page: OVHcloud bm-m1 is a bare metal compute configuration belonging to the Metal server family, running on the KVM hypervisor. The machine is powered by an x86_64 processor delivering 8 dedicated vCPUs with a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. Compute tasks are supported by 64 GB of system RAM, maintaining a resource allocation of 8 GB per virtual core. Storage is provided locally through an integrated 1920 GB NVMe SSD, ensuring low-latency access to disk operations directly attached to the host. The server features a baseline network capacity of 1 Gbps and includes no complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Dedicated GPU accelerators are not present in this configuration.

With dedicated CPU cores running at 3.7 GHz, the server ensures consistent compute execution without the noisy-neighbor interference typical of multi-tenant environments. The 1:8 core-to-memory ratio provides sufficient headroom for workloads that maintain large working sets in RAM, while the 1920 GB NVMe drive provides direct access to fast non-volatile storage. The network interface baseline of 1 Gbps offers standard host connectivity, though it requires consideration when deploying distributed applications requiring high inter-node data exchange throughput.

The hardware profile represents a practical configuration for environments requiring dedicated memory density and rapid local disk storage without the added expense of GPU accelerators. By combining 64 GB of memory and fast NVMe storage with 8 dedicated cores, the bm-m1 instance fits relational databases, in-memory key-value stores, transactional enterprise systems, and mid-tier extract-transform-load workloads.
description: OVHcloud bm-m1 is a bare metal server within the Metal family designed for memory-intensive and data-centric workloads. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via KVM, the system provides 8 dedicated vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. Memory capacity is configured at 64 GB, establishing an 8 GB per core ratio that aligns with memory-optimized requirements. For high-speed local data persistence, the instance bundles 1920 GB of NVMe SSD storage, eliminating the need for remote network storage volumes for primary workloads. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline throughput of 1 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included by default. The configuration lacks GPU hardware accelerators, directing its resource profile toward backend database hosting, in-memory caching, extract-transform-load processing, and analytical applications that demand high single-threaded clock speed combined with dense local memory and storage.
